title: Separate useful load paths from fracture work and consumed pullout inventory
statement: For the declared equal-load interface with n paths per area, each sustaining peak force f>0 and dissipating U_b>0 in exactly one scission, sigma_max=n*f and Gamma_direct=n*U_b, hence Gamma_direct/sigma_max=U_b/f. At MINIMALLY sufficient n=sigma_target/f, Gamma_direct=sigma_target*U_b/f; a target traction alone does not bound actual n or general toughness. Ideal constant traction over displacement ell gives Gamma=sigma*ell.

requires: The exact equal-load single-scission class, with known effective path count, per-path force/work and no omitted dissipation.
For the pullout budget, ideal alignment, constant traction/sliding force, distinct cylindrical fibres and actual useful sliding inventory; all parameters are supplied.
provides: For the declared equal-load interface with n paths per area, each sustaining peak force f>0 and dissipating U_b>0 in exactly one scission, sigma_max=n*f and Gamma_direct=n*U_b, hence Gamma_direct/sigma_max=U_b/f. At MINIMALLY sufficient n=sigma_target/f, Gamma_direct=sigma_target*U_b/f; a target traction alone does not bound actual n or general toughness. Ideal constant traction over displacement ell gives Gamma=sigma*ell.
assumptions: This is not a universal upper bound on interface toughness at a given required traction; more paths or other dissipation can change it.
Ideal packing/material budgets and stored energy are not measured wet fracture or fatigue properties.
costs: Pay actual load-bearing fibre mass/volume, anchoring, sliding displacement and every consumed irreversible tail; repeated loading needs renewable dissipation or more inventory.
contract.units: n m^-2,f N,U_b J,sigma Pa,Gamma J/m^2; U_b/f,ell,r,h lengths; E Pa,rho kg/m^3.
contract.obstruction: Acquire actual wet load paths and an energy-dissipating region before inferring fracture resistance from successful attachment.

body: Eliminate the same n between force and one-scission work budgets. Additional deformation/dissipation or a different path density changes the result. Linear-elastic stored energy sigma^2*h/(2E) belongs to its declared geometry and is not automatically crack release or fatigue threshold. For aligned cylindrical fibres of radius r at constant sliding force f_s, required density=sigma/f_s, ideal area occupancy phi=sigma*pi*r^2/f_s and useful sliding length ell=Gamma/sigma. Necessary nonoverlap is phi<=1 (not sufficiency); dry mass/area=rho*phi*ell under complete utilization. Irreversible sliding spends the available tail; repeated equal-work events need proportional total sliding inventory unless a genuine reset/recovery operation replenishes it. Molecular docking cannot silently supply that larger deformation zone.
